sources.entry: CocoaRestClient - Native Apple macOS app for testing HTTP/REST endpoints.

summary.one_liner: CocoaRestClient is a lightweight native macOS app for testing and debugging HTTP/REST endpoints, positioned as curl with a simple UI.
summary.what_it_does: The app sends GET, PUT, POST, DELETE and HEAD requests with arbitrary bodies and custom headers. It lets you edit URL parameters in a table and set HTTP basic or digest auth. Responses in XML, JSON, and MsgPack are auto-formatted (pretty printed), and response headers are displayed along with response latency. Requests can be saved in a sidebar organized into folders, and POST/PUT input can be entered as raw text or key/value pairs. It also supports multipart/form-data file uploads and form encoding, plus a unified diff tool for comparing response bodies.
use_cases: pretty printing JSON or XML responses
saving frequently used request bodies and headers
how_to_run: pod install (only when building from source, in the project directory)
notable: Pretty printing for XML, JSON, and MsgPack responses
Sidebar for saving requests with folder organization
Unified diff tool for response bodies
caveats: Source build depends on a GitHub-hosted CocoaPods dependency, so building requires a GitHub account with a registered public key
Described as a Mac OS X app, so it runs only on macOS
README is brief and does not state a current maintenance status
